newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh sees benefits in sub-regional trade bloc.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh sees benefits in sub-regional trade bloc.

text.p: A senior Foreign Ministry official said on Wednesday a sub-regional trading bloc proposed by Bangladesh and India would boost the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).

"Certainly it (a new bloc) is not going to be formed at the expense of SAARC," Farooq Sobhan told a meeting of the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh. "However, the proposal has created some confusions," he added.

The bloc comprising Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Bhutan -- four of the seven SAARC member-states -- was proposed during the two-day visit to Dhaka by Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who returned home on Tuesday.
Maldives, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are other members of the SAARC, which has been criticised as ineffective mainly due to militant rivalry between India and Pakistan.
"There are things that we can't do well by all seven members, but those may be done by three or four," Sobhan said.
